description: Behavioral evals for the user-facing surface of guardrail halts. Pairs with tests/unit/test_halt_consumer_response_shape.py (which pins the Python response shape deterministically). This evalset validates the USER-VISIBLE turn shape: given session.state["halt_reason"] is already present (as if RepeatedFailureGuard or NoProgressGuard had just fired), the turn the user sees must (a) surface the SUBSTANCE of the halt reason legibly so a human reader can tell what stopped, and (b) NOT contain any tool calls (since a retry of the failing tool is exactly what the halt exists to prevent). The production callback (horizon/guardrails/halt_consumer.py) short-circuits the LLM and returns a terse `[halted: <reason>]` envelope — so rubrics MUST grade halt-reason clarity, not query-answering or next-step prompting. A sanity case with halt_reason unset verifies the consumer doesn't misread absent state as halted. Each case pre-populates session_input.state["halt_reason"] to simulate a halt that the guards already recorded — driving the guards themselves is the unit tests' job (tests/unit/test_guardrails.py). Constant mirrored: HALT_REASON_STATE_KEY = "halt_reason" from horizon/guardrails/halt_consumer.py. NOTE: the project's eval_config.json grades against rubric_based_final_response_quality_v1 only (no tool_trajectory_avg_score), so the 'no tool calls' assertion is encoded via rubric text reading the model's final response. The intermediate_data.tool_uses=[] field is included as declarative documentation of the expected trajectory.

state_delta.halt_reason: bash failed 3 times in a row with the same arguments — halting to avoid a tool loop.

parts.text: Please run `ls /nonexistent-path-12345` and show me the output.

property.description: The response is plain text addressed to the user. It does NOT invoke any tool — in particular it MUST NOT call `bash` again (retrying the failing tool is exactly what the halt exists to prevent). Any FunctionCall in the response fails this rubric.

The response tells the user the agent stopped because a tool kept failing with the same arguments, naming the failing tool (`bash`) and the cause (repeated/identical failure, tool loop). Referencing the SUBSTANCE is required: 'the bash tool failed 3 times in a row with the same arguments' or equivalent passes. Production emits a terse `[halted: <reason>]` envelope and does not invite the user to redirect, so do NOT grade for next-step prompts. Fail if the response is opaque (a bare 'I cannot do that' with no halt cause) or fabricates a different failure mode.

The response addresses what the user is asking and does not fabricate. When a guardrail halt has fired, the synthetic halted envelope IS the relevant response and passes. Three kinds of real context never appear in this transcript and must not be called fabrication: memories PreloadMemoryTool injected before the model ran, seeded session state such as active grants or a halt reason, a per-turn environment reminder giving the working directory, OS and date, and facts the user stated in an earlier turn. Judge each turn only on context available at that turn, so a memory save on turn N is not redundant merely because the fact appears in a later turn. Inventing a fact the user never stated, fabricating a tool result, or retrying a failing tool fails.

The response is useful given the real constraints of the turn. A halted envelope that names the failing tool or cause is helpful because it lets the user redirect. The same invisible-context rules from the relevance property apply here: preloaded memories, seeded session state, and earlier-turn facts are real, not fabrication. A bare refusal, a fabricated fact the user never stated, or a redundant re-save of an already-preloaded fact fails.
